subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should trusted hook-agent integrations get an explicit persistent session mode, or should `/hooks/agent` remain isolated-only with docs clarifying that stable `sessionKey` is routing metadata rather than transcript continuity?
rationale: Source inspection proves the requested behavior is still missing, but the fix changes public hook API/config surface and session security boundaries, so maintainer intent is needed before treating the linked PR direction as the permanent product contract.

options.title: Accept Explicit Persistent Mode
options.body: Review and land a narrow version of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 that preserves isolated defaults and gates persistent reuse through hook auth, allowed prefixes, and agent/session policy.

options.title: Keep Hooks Isolated-Only
options.body: Reject the persistent-mode direction and update docs to say `/hooks/agent` cannot preserve transcript continuity through `sessionKey`.

options.title: Design Broader Session Identity
options.body: Pause the linked PR and define a wider deterministic session identity model for trusted hooks before adding public config surface.

recommendation.title: Accept Explicit Persistent Mode
recommendation.body: Review and land a narrow version of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 that preserves isolated defaults and gates persistent reuse through hook auth, allowed prefixes, and agent/session policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter supplied the latest product-direction comment for this exact issue and current-line history points through his recent main commit.
